author: Nixawk
auxiliary_scanner/http/linknat_vos_trave.description:
This module attempts to test whether a file traversal vulnerability
          is present in version of linknat vos2009/vos3000
auxiliary_scanner/http/linknat_vos_trave.name: Linknat Vos Manager Traversal

author: Michael Messner <devnull@s3cur1ty.de>
auxiliary_scanner/http/linksys_e1500_tra.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal vulnerability which is present in
        different Linksys home routers, like the E1500.
auxiliary_scanner/http/linksys_e1500_tra.name: Linksys E1500 Directory Traversal Vulnerability

author: Kingcope
xanda
auxiliary_scanner/http/litespeed_source_.description:
This module exploits a source code disclosure/download vulnerability in
        versions 4.0.14 and prior of LiteSpeed.
auxiliary_scanner/http/litespeed_source_.name: LiteSpeed Source Code Disclosure/Download

author: Spencer McIntyre
RageLtMan <rageltman@sempervictus>
auxiliary_scanner/http/log4shell_scanner.description:
Versions of Apache Log4j2 impacted by CVE-2021-44228 which allow JNDI features used in configuration,
        log messages, and parameters, do not protect against attacker controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints.

        This module will scan an HTTP end point for the Log4Shell vulnerability by injecting a format message that will
        trigger an LDAP connection to Metasploit. This module is a generic scanner and is only capable of identifying
        instances that are vulnerable via one of the pre-determined HTTP request injection points. These points include
        HTTP headers and the HTTP request path.

        Known impacted software includes Apache Struts 2, VMWare VCenter, Apache James, Apache Solr, Apache Druid,
        Apache JSPWiki, Apache OFBiz.
auxiliary_scanner/http/log4shell_scanner.name: Log4Shell HTTP Scanner

author: et <et@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/lucky_punch.description:
This module implements the mass SQL injection attack in
          use lately by concatenation of HTML string that forces a persistent
          XSS attack to redirect user browser to an attacker controller website.
auxiliary_scanner/http/lucky_punch.name: HTTP Microsoft SQL Injection Table XSS Infection

author: Nikolas Sotiriu
auxiliary_scanner/http/majordomo2_direct.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal vulnerability present in
        the _list_file_get() function of Majordomo2 (help function). By default, this
        module will attempt to download the Majordomo config.pl file.
auxiliary_scanner/http/majordomo2_direct.name: Majordomo2 _list_file_get() Directory Traversal

author: sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/manageengine_desk.description: This module will attempt to authenticate to a ManageEngine Desktop Central.
auxiliary_scanner/http/manageengine_desk.name: ManageEngine Desktop Central Login Utility

author: rgod
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/manageengine_devi.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal vulnerability found in ManageEngine
          DeviceExpert's ScheduleResultViewer Servlet.  This is done by using
          "..\..\..\..\..\..\..\..\..\..\" in the path in order to retrieve a file on a
          vulnerable machine.  Please note that the SSL option is required in order to send
          HTTP requests.
auxiliary_scanner/http/manageengine_devi.name: ManageEngine DeviceExpert 5.6 ScheduleResultViewer FileName Traversal

author: Pedro Ribeiro <pedrib@gmail.com>
bcoles <bcoles@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/manageengine_devi.description:
This module extracts usernames and salted MD5 password hashes
          from ManageEngine DeviceExpert version 5.9 build 5980 and prior.

          This module has been tested successfully on DeviceExpert
          version 5.9.7 build 5970.
auxiliary_scanner/http/manageengine_devi.name: ManageEngine DeviceExpert User Credentials

author: blkhtc0rp
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/manageengine_secu.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal flaw found in ManageEngine
          SecurityManager Plus 5.5 or less.  When handling a file download request,
          the DownloadServlet class fails to properly check the 'f' parameter, which
          can be abused to read any file outside the virtual directory.
auxiliary_scanner/http/manageengine_secu.name: ManageEngine SecurityManager Plus 5.5 Directory Traversal

author: Daniel Franke
juan vazquez <juan.vazquez@metasploit.com>
Christian Mehlmauer <FireFart@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/mediawiki_svg_fil.description:
This module attempts to read a remote file from the server using a vulnerability
        in the way MediaWiki handles SVG files. The vulnerability occurs while trying to
        expand external entities with the SYSTEM identifier. In order to work MediaWiki must
        be configured to accept upload of SVG files. If anonymous uploads are allowed the
        username and password aren't required, otherwise they are. This module has been
        tested successfully on MediaWiki 1.19.4, 1.20.3 on Ubuntu 10.04 and Ubuntu 12.10.
        Older versions were also tested but do not seem to be vulnerable to this vulnerability.
        The following MediaWiki requirements must be met: File upload must be enabled,
        $wgFileExtensions[] must include 'svg', $wgSVGConverter must be set to something
        other than 'false'.
auxiliary_scanner/http/mediawiki_svg_fil.name: MediaWiki SVG XML Entity Expansion Remote File Access

author: Karn Ganeshen <KarnGaneshen@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/meteocontrol_webl.description: This module exploits an authentication bypass vulnerability in Meteocontrol WEBLog appliances (software version < May 2016 release) to extract Administrator password for the device management portal.
auxiliary_scanner/http/meteocontrol_webl.name: Meteocontrol WEBlog Password Extractor

author: diablohorn <diablohorn@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/mod_negotiation_b.description:
This module performs a brute force attack in order to discover existing files on a
          server which uses mod_negotiation. If the filename is found, the IP address and the
          files found will be displayed.
auxiliary_scanner/http/mod_negotiation_b.name: Apache HTTPD mod_negotiation Filename Bruter

author: diablohorn <diablohorn@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/mod_negotiation_s.description:
This module scans the webserver of the given host(s) for the existence of mod_negotiate.
          If the webserver has mod_negotiation enabled, the IP address will be displayed.
auxiliary_scanner/http/mod_negotiation_s.name: Apache HTTPD mod_negotiation Scanner

author: et <et@metasploit.com>
aushack <patrick@osisecurity.com.au>
auxiliary_scanner/http/ms09_020_webdav_u.description:
This module attempts to to bypass authentication using the WebDAV IIS6
          Unicode vulnerability discovered by Kingcope. The vulnerability appears
          to be exploitable where WebDAV is enabled on the IIS6 server, and any
          protected folder requires either Basic, Digest or NTLM authentication.
auxiliary_scanner/http/ms09_020_webdav_u.name: MS09-020 IIS6 WebDAV Unicode Authentication Bypass

author: Rich Whitcroft <rwhitcroft@gmail.com>
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
Sunny Neo <sunny.neo@centurioninfosec.sg>
auxiliary_scanner/http/ms15_034_http_sys.description:
This module dumps memory contents using a crafted Range header and affects only
          Windows 8.1, Server 2012, and Server 2012R2. Note that if the target
          is running in VMware Workstation, this module has a high likelihood
          of resulting in BSOD; however, VMware ESX and non-virtualized hosts
          seem stable. Using a larger target file should result in more memory
          being dumped, and SSL seems to produce more data as well.
auxiliary_scanner/http/ms15_034_http_sys.name: MS15-034 HTTP Protocol Stack Request Handling HTTP.SYS Memory Information Disclosure

author: Nicholas Starke <starke.nicholas@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/mybook_live_login.description: This module simply attempts to login to a Western Digital MyBook Live instance using a specific user/pass.
auxiliary_scanner/http/mybook_live_login.name: Western Digital MyBook Live Login Utility

author: Erik Wynter
auxiliary_scanner/http/nagios_xi_scanner.description:
The module detects the version of Nagios XI applications and
        suggests matching exploit modules based on the version number.
        Since Nagios XI applications only reveal the version to authenticated
        users, valid credentials for a Nagios XI account are required.
        Alternatively, it is possible to provide a specific Nagios XI version
        number via the `VERSION` option. In that case, the module simply
        suggests matching exploit modules and does not probe the target(s).
auxiliary_scanner/http/nagios_xi_scanner.name: Nagios XI Scanner

author: chebuya
msutovsky-r7
auxiliary_scanner/http/netalertx_file_re.description: This module exploits improper authentication in logs.php endpoint. An unathenticated attacker can request log file and read any file due path traversal vulnerability.
auxiliary_scanner/http/netalertx_file_re.name: NetAlertX File Read Vulnerability

author: Luigi Auriemma
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/netdecision_trave.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal bug in NetDecision's
          TrafficGrapherServer.exe service.  This is done by using "...\" in
          the path to retrieve a file on a vulnerable machine.
auxiliary_scanner/http/netdecision_trave.name: NetDecision NOCVision Server Directory Traversal

author: Michael Messner <devnull@s3cur1ty.de>
auxiliary_scanner/http/netgear_sph200d_t.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal vulnerability which is present in
        Netgear SPH200D Skype telephone.
auxiliary_scanner/http/netgear_sph200d_t.name: Netgear SPH200D Directory Traversal Vulnerability

author: Tiago Ferreira <tiago.ccna@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/nginx_source_disc.description:
This module exploits a source code disclosure/download vulnerability in
        versions 0.7 and 0.8 of the nginx web server. Versions 0.7.66 and 0.8.40
        correct this vulnerability.
auxiliary_scanner/http/nginx_source_disc.name: Nginx Source Code Disclosure/Download

author: juan vazquez <juan.vazquez@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/novell_file_repor.description:
NFRAgent.exe, a component of Novell File Reporter (NFR), allows remote attackers to retrieve
        arbitrary text files via a directory traversal while handling requests to /FSF/CMD
        with an FSFUI record with UICMD 126. This module has been tested successfully
        against NFR Agent 1.0.4.3 (File Reporter 1.0.2) and NFR Agent 1.0.3.22 (File
        Reporter 1.0.1).
auxiliary_scanner/http/novell_file_repor.name: NFR Agent FSFUI Record Arbitrary Remote File Access

author: juan vazquez <juan.vazquez@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/novell_file_repor.description:
NFRAgent.exe, a component of Novell File Reporter (NFR), allows remote attackers to retrieve
        arbitrary files via a request to /FSF/CMD with a SRS Record with OPERATION 4 and
        CMD 103, specifying a full pathname. This module has been tested successfully
        against NFR Agent 1.0.4.3 (File Reporter 1.0.2) and NFR Agent 1.0.3.22 (File
        Reporter 1.0.1).
auxiliary_scanner/http/novell_file_repor.name: NFR Agent SRS Record Arbitrary Remote File Access

author: steponequit
Andrea Micalizzi (aka rgod)
auxiliary_scanner/http/novell_mdm_creds.description:
This module attempts to pull the administrator credentials from
        a vulnerable Novell Zenworks MDM server.
auxiliary_scanner/http/novell_mdm_creds.name: Novell Zenworks Mobile Device Management Admin Credentials

author: Brandon Knight
auxiliary_scanner/http/ntlm_info_enumera.description:
This module makes requests to resources on the target server in
        an attempt to find resources which permit NTLM authentication. For
        resources which permit NTLM authentication, a blank NTLM type 1 message
        is sent to enumerate a type 2 message from the target server. The type
        2 message is then parsed for information such as the Active Directory
        domain and NetBIOS name.  A single URI can be specified with TARGET_URI
        and/or a file of URIs can be specified with TARGET_URIS_FILE (default).
auxiliary_scanner/http/ntlm_info_enumera.name: Host Information Enumeration via NTLM Authentication

author: James Otten <jamesotten1@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/octopusdeploy_log.description:
This module simply attempts to login to an Octopus Deploy server using a specific
        username and password. It has been confirmed to work on version 3.4.4
auxiliary_scanner/http/octopusdeploy_log.name: Octopus Deploy Login Utility

author: Not So Attractive <github.com/nsa>
auxiliary_scanner/http/onion_omega2_logi.description: OnionOS login scanner module for Onion Omega2 devices.
auxiliary_scanner/http/onion_omega2_logi.name: Onion Omega2 Login Brute-Force

author: Matteo Cantoni <goony@nothink.org>
auxiliary_scanner/http/open_proxy.description:
Checks if an HTTP proxy is open. False positive are avoided
          verifying the HTTP return code and matching a pattern.
          The CONNECT method is verified only the return code.
          HTTP headers are shown regarding the use of proxy or load balancer.
auxiliary_scanner/http/open_proxy.name: HTTP Open Proxy Detection

author: Karn Ganeshen <KarnGaneshen@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/openmind_messageo.description:
This module scans for OpenMind Message-OS provisioning web login portal, and
          performs a login brute force attack to identify valid credentials.
auxiliary_scanner/http/openmind_messageo.name: OpenMind Message-OS Portal Login Brute Force Utility

author: sjanusz-r7
auxiliary_scanner/http/opnsense_login.description: This module performs login attempts against a Deciso B.V OPNSense router webpage to bruteforce possible credentials.
auxiliary_scanner/http/opnsense_login.name: OPNSense Login Scanner

author: CG <cg@carnal0wnage.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/options.description: Display available HTTP options for each system
auxiliary_scanner/http/options.name: HTTP Options Detection

author: Oliver Gruskovnjak
auxiliary_scanner/http/oracle_demantra_d.description:
This module exploits a database credentials leak found in Oracle Demantra 12.2.1 in
          combination with an authentication bypass. This way an unauthenticated user can retrieve
          the database name, username and password on any vulnerable machine.
auxiliary_scanner/http/oracle_demantra_d.name: Oracle Demantra Database Credentials Leak

author: Oliver Gruskovnjak
auxiliary_scanner/http/oracle_demantra_f.description:
This module exploits a file download vulnerability found in Oracle
          Demantra 12.2.1 in combination with an authentication bypass. By
          combining these exposures, an unauthenticated user can retrieve any file
          on the system by referencing the full file path to any file a vulnerable
          machine.
auxiliary_scanner/http/oracle_demantra_f.name: Oracle Demantra Arbitrary File Retrieval with Authentication Bypass

author: Karn Ganeshen <KarnGaneshen@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/oracle_ilom_login.description:
This module scans for Oracle Integrated Lights Out Manager (ILO) login portal, and
          performs a login brute force attack to identify valid credentials.
auxiliary_scanner/http/oracle_ilom_login.name: Oracle ILO Manager Login Brute Force Utility

author: Rich Whitcroft
auxiliary_scanner/http/owa_ews_login.description:
This module attempts to log in to the Exchange Web Services, often
        exposed at https://example.com/ews/, using NTLM authentication. This
        method is faster and simpler than traditional form-based logins.

        In most cases, all you need to set is RHOSTS and some combination of
        user/pass files; the autodiscovery should find the location of the NTLM
        authentication point as well as the AD domain, and use them accordingly.
auxiliary_scanner/http/owa_ews_login.name: OWA Exchange Web Services (EWS) Login Scanner

author: Nate Power
auxiliary_scanner/http/owa_iis_internal_.description:
This module tests vulnerable IIS HTTP header file paths on Microsoft
        Exchange OWA 2003 and CAS 2007, 2010, and 2013 servers.
auxiliary_scanner/http/owa_iis_internal_.name: Outlook Web App (OWA) / Client Access Server (CAS) IIS HTTP Internal IP Disclosure

author: Vitor Moreira
Spencer McIntyre
SecureState R&D Team
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
Brandon Knight
Pete (Bokojan) Arzamendi
Nate Power
Chapman (R3naissance) Schleiss
Andrew Smith
auxiliary_scanner/http/owa_login.description: This module tests credentials on OWA 2003, 2007, 2010, 2013, and 2016 servers.
auxiliary_scanner/http/owa_login.name: Outlook Web App (OWA) Brute Force Utility

author: sjanusz-r7
auxiliary_scanner/http/pfsense_login.description: This module performs login attempts against a Netgate pfSense router webpage to bruteforce possible credentials.
auxiliary_scanner/http/pfsense_login.name: pfSense Login Scanner

author: Shelby Pace
auxiliary_scanner/http/phpmyadmin_login.description: This module will attempt to authenticate to PhpMyAdmin.
auxiliary_scanner/http/phpmyadmin_login.name: PhpMyAdmin Login Scanner

author: Karn Ganeshen <KarnGaneshen@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/pocketpad_login.description:
This module scans for PocketPAD login portal, and
          performs a login bruteforce attack to identify valid credentials.
auxiliary_scanner/http/pocketpad_login.name: PocketPAD Login Bruteforce Force Utility

author: Stefan Schiller
msutovsky-r7
auxiliary_scanner/http/pretalx_file_read.description: This module exploits functionality in Pretalx that export conference schedule as zipped file. The Pretalx will iteratively include any file referenced by any HTML tag and does not properly check the path of the file, which can lead to arbitrary file read. The module requires credentials that allow schedule export, schedule release and approval of proposals. Additionally, module requires conference name and URL for media files.
auxiliary_scanner/http/pretalx_file_read.name: Pretalx Arbitrary File Read/Limited File Write

author: et <et@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/prev_dir_same_nam.description:
This module identifies files in the first parent directory with same name as
          the given directory path. Example: Test /backup/files/ will look for the
          following files /backup/files.ext .
auxiliary_scanner/http/prev_dir_same_nam.name: HTTP Previous Directory File Scanner

author: Karn Ganeshen <KarnGaneshen@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/radware_appdirect.description:
This module scans for Radware AppDirector's web login portal, and performs login brute force
          to identify valid credentials.
auxiliary_scanner/http/radware_appdirect.name: Radware AppDirector Bruteforce Login Utility

author: jjarmoc
hdm <x@hdm.io>
auxiliary_scanner/http/rails_json_yaml_s.description:
This module attempts to identify Ruby on Rails instances vulnerable to
          an arbitrary object instantiation flaw in the JSON request processor.
auxiliary_scanner/http/rails_json_yaml_s.name: Ruby on Rails JSON Processor YAML Deserialization Scanner

author: Gregory Man <man.gregory@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/rails_mass_assign.description:
This module scans Ruby On Rails sites for
          models with attributes not protected by attr_protected or attr_accessible.
          After attempting to assign a non-existent field, the default rails with
          active_record setup will raise an ActiveRecord::UnknownAttributeError
          exception, and reply with HTTP code 500.
auxiliary_scanner/http/rails_mass_assign.name: Ruby On Rails Attributes Mass Assignment Scanner

author: hdm <x@hdm.io>
jjarmoc
auxiliary_scanner/http/rails_xml_yaml_sc.description:
This module attempts to identify Ruby on Rails instances vulnerable to
          an arbitrary object instantiation flaw in the XML request processor.
auxiliary_scanner/http/rails_xml_yaml_sc.name: Ruby on Rails XML Processor YAML Deserialization Scanner

author: Matthew Dunn
auxiliary_scanner/http/rdp_web_login.description:
Enumerate valid usernames and passwords against a Microsoft RDP Web Client
        by attempting authentication and performing a timing based check
        against the provided username.
auxiliary_scanner/http/rdp_web_login.name: Microsoft RDP Web Client Login Enumeration

author: et <et@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/replace_ext.description:
This module identifies the existence of additional files
          by modifying the extension of an existing file.
auxiliary_scanner/http/replace_ext.name: HTTP File Extension Scanner

author: chao-mu
auxiliary_scanner/http/rewrite_proxy_byp.description:
Scan for poorly configured reverse proxy servers.
        By default, this module attempts to force the server to make
        a request with an invalid domain name. Then, if the bypass
        is successful, the server will look it up and of course fail,
        then responding with a status code 502. A baseline status code
        is always established and if that baseline matches your test
        status code, the injection attempt does not occur.
        "set VERBOSE true" if you are paranoid and want to catch potential
        false negatives. Works best against Apache and mod_rewrite
auxiliary_scanner/http/rewrite_proxy_byp.name: Apache Reverse Proxy Bypass Vulnerability Scanner

author: Karn Ganeshen <KarnGaneshen@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/rfcode_reader_enu.description:
This module simply attempts to login to a RFCode Reader web interface.
          Please note that by default there is no authentication. In such a case, password brute force will not be performed.
          If there is authentication configured, the module will attempt to find valid login credentials and capture device information.
auxiliary_scanner/http/rfcode_reader_enu.name: RFCode Reader Web Interface Login / Bruteforce Utility

author: localh0t
Roberto Soares Espreto <robertoespreto@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/rips_traversal.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal vulnerability in the RIPS Scanner v0.54,
          allowing to read arbitrary files with the web server privileges.
auxiliary_scanner/http/rips_traversal.name: RIPS Scanner Directory Traversal

author: Gregory DRAPERI <gregory.draper_at_gmail.com>
h00die
auxiliary_scanner/http/riverbed_steelhea.description:
This module exploits an authenticated arbitrary file read in the log module's filter engine.
          SteelHead VCX (VCX255U) version 9.6.0a was confirmed as vulnerable.
auxiliary_scanner/http/riverbed_steelhea.name: Riverbed SteelHead VCX File Read

author: et <et@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/robots_txt.description: Detect robots.txt files and analyze its content
auxiliary_scanner/http/robots_txt.name: HTTP Robots.txt Content Scanner

author: Aaron Meese <@ajmeese7>
Jamie Hill-Daniel <@clubby789>
auxiliary_scanner/http/rpyc_rce.description:
This module allows remote command execution on RPyC versions 4.1.0 and 4.1.1.
        You will be able to execute a specified command on the target machine as
        the user running the RPyC service and view the output.
auxiliary_scanner/http/rpyc_rce.name: RPyC 4.1.0 through 4.1.1 Remote Command Execution

author: Osirys <osirys@autistici.org>
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/s40_traversal.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal vulnerability found in S40 CMS.
          The flaw is due to the 'page' function not properly handling the $pid parameter,
          which allows a malicious user to load an arbitrary file path.
auxiliary_scanner/http/s40_traversal.name: S40 0.4.2 CMS Directory Traversal Vulnerability

author: Joshua Abraham <jabra@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/sap_businessobjec.description:
This module attempts to bruteforce SAP BusinessObjects users.
        The dswsbobje interface is only used to verify valid credentials for CmcApp.
        Therefore, any valid credentials that have been identified can be leveraged by
        logging into CmcApp.
auxiliary_scanner/http/sap_businessobjec.name: SAP BusinessObjects User Bruteforcer

author: Joshua Abraham <jabra@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/sap_businessobjec.description: This module simply attempts to bruteforce SAP BusinessObjects users by using CmcApp.
auxiliary_scanner/http/sap_businessobjec.name: SAP BusinessObjects Web User Bruteforcer

author: Joshua Abraham <jabra@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/sap_businessobjec.description:
This module simply attempts to enumerate SAP BusinessObjects
        users. The dswsbobje interface is only used to verify valid
        users for CmcApp. Therefore, any valid users that have been
        identified can be leveraged by logging into CmcApp.
auxiliary_scanner/http/sap_businessobjec.name: SAP BusinessObjects User Enumeration

author: Joshua Abraham <jabra@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/sap_businessobjec.description: This module simply attempts to identify the version of SAP BusinessObjects.
auxiliary_scanner/http/sap_businessobjec.name: SAP BusinessObjects Version Detection

author: et <et@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/scraper.description: Scrape defined data from a specific web page based on a regular expression
auxiliary_scanner/http/scraper.name: HTTP Page Scraper

author: Karn Ganeshen <KarnGaneshen@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/sentry_cdu_enum.description:
This module scans for ServerTech's Sentry Switched CDU (Cabinet Power
          Distribution Unit) web login portals, and performs login brute force
          to identify valid credentials.
auxiliary_scanner/http/sentry_cdu_enum.name: Sentry Switched CDU Bruteforce Login Utility

author: xistence <xistence@0x90.nl>
auxiliary_scanner/http/servicedesk_plus_.description:
This module exploits an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability found in ManageEngine
          ServiceDesk Plus build 9110 and lower. The module will retrieve any file on the filesystem
          with the same privileges as Support Center Plus is running. On Windows, files can be retrieved
          with SYSTEM privileges. The issue has been resolved in ServiceDesk Plus build 91111 (issue SD-60283).
auxiliary_scanner/http/servicedesk_plus_.name: ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus Path Traversal

author: Karn Ganeshen <KarnGaneshen@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/sevone_enum.description:
This module scans for SevOne Network Performance Management System Application,
          finds its version, and performs login brute force to identify valid credentials.
auxiliary_scanner/http/sevone_enum.name: SevOne Network Performance Management Application Brute Force Login Utility

author: CwG GeNiuS
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/simple_webserver_.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal vulnerability found in
          Simple Web Server 2.3-RC1.
auxiliary_scanner/http/simple_webserver_.name: Simple Web Server 2.3-RC1 Directory Traversal

author: horizon3ai
imjdl
jheysel-r7
auxiliary_scanner/http/simplehelp_toolbo.description:
There exists a path traversal vulnerability in the /toolbox-resource endpoint that enables unauthenticated
          remote attackers to download arbitrary files from the SimpleHelp server via crafted HTTP requests
auxiliary_scanner/http/simplehelp_toolbo.name: SimpleHelp Path Traversal Vulnerability CVE-2024-57727

author: Zach Wikholm <kestrel@trylinux.us>
John Matherly <jmath@shodan.io>
Dan Farmer <zen@fish2.com>
hdm <x@hdm.io>
auxiliary_scanner/http/smt_ipmi_49152_ex.description:
This module abuses a file exposure vulnerability accessible through the web interface
          on port 49152 of Supermicro Onboard IPMI controllers.  The vulnerability allows an attacker
          to obtain detailed device information and download data files containing the clear-text
          usernames and passwords for the controller. In May of 2014, at least 30,000 unique IPs
          were exposed to the internet with this vulnerability.
auxiliary_scanner/http/smt_ipmi_49152_ex.name: Supermicro Onboard IPMI Port 49152 Sensitive File Exposure

author: hdm <x@hdm.io>
juan vazquez <juan.vazquez@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/http/smt_ipmi_cgi_scan.description:

          accessible through the web interface of Supermicro Onboard IPMI controllers.  The vulnerability
          is present due to a lack of sanitization of the url_name parameter. This allows an attacker with

author: willis
0x44434241
auxiliary_scanner/http/squid_pivot_scann.description:
A exposed Squid proxy will usually allow an attacker to make requests on
        their behalf. If misconfigured, this may give the attacker information
        about devices that they cannot normally reach. For example, an attacker
        may be able to make requests for internal IP addresses against an open
        Squid proxy exposed to the Internet, therefore performing a port scan
        against the internal network.

        The `auxiliary/scanner/http/open_proxy` module can be used to test for
        open proxies, though a Squid proxy does not have to be on the open
        Internet in order to allow for pivoting (e.g. an Intranet Squid proxy
        which allows the attack to pivot to another part of the internal
        network).

        This module will not be able to scan network ranges or ports denied by
        Squid ACLs. Fortunately it is possible to detect whether a host was up
        and the port was closed, or if the request was blocked by an ACL, based
        on the response Squid gives. This feedback is provided to the user in
        meterpreter `VERBOSE` output, otherwise only open and permitted ports
        are printed.
auxiliary_scanner/http/squid_pivot_scann.name: Squid Proxy Port Scanner

author: Troy Rose <troy@osisecurity.com.au>
aushack <patrick@osisecurity.com.au>
auxiliary_scanner/http/squiz_matrix_user.description:

          the Squiz Matrix and MySource Matrix CMS by sending GET requests for asset IDs
          e.g. ?a=14 and searching for a valid username eg "~root" or "~test" which
          is prefixed by a "~" in the response. It will also try to GET the users
          full name or description, or other information. You may wish to modify
          ASSETBEGIN and ASSETEND values for greater results, or set VERBOSE.
          Information gathered may be used for later bruteforce attacks.
auxiliary_scanner/http/squiz_matrix_user.name: Squiz Matrix User Enumeration Scanner

auxiliary_scanner/http/strapi_3_password.description:

auxiliary_scanner/http/support_center_pl.description:

auxiliary_scanner/http/surgenews_user_cr.description:

          This module extracts the administrator username and password, and
          the usernames and passwords or password hashes for all users.

          This module has been tested successfully on SurgeNews version
          2.0a-13 on Windows 7 SP 1 and 2.0a-12 on Ubuntu Linux.
auxiliary_scanner/http/surgenews_user_cr.name: SurgeNews User Credentials

author: Jan Rude
auxiliary_scanner/http/syncovery_linux_t.description:
This module attempts to brute-force a valid session token for the Syncovery File Sync & Backup Software Web-GUI
          by generating all possible tokens, for every second between 'DateTime.now' and the given X day(s).
          By default today and yesterday (DAYS = 1) will be checked. If a valid session token is found, the module stops.
          The vulnerability exists, because in Syncovery session tokens are basically just base64(m/d/Y H:M:S) at the time
          of the login instead of a random token.
          If a user does not log out (Syncovery v8.x has no logout) session tokens will remain valid until reboot.
auxiliary_scanner/http/syncovery_linux_t.name: Syncovery For Linux Web-GUI Session Token Brute-Forcer

          by sending GET requests for the forgot password URL.

          These count as login attempts, and the default is 10 logins in 5min to
          get a permanent block.  Set delay accordingly to avoid this, as default
          is permanent.
          Vulnerable DSMs are:
          DSM 6.1 < 6.1.3-15152
          DSM 6.0 < 6.0.3-8754-4
          DSM 5.2 < 5.2-5967-04

author: Spencer McIntyre

      retrieve the username and password for the administrative XML-RPC
      interface, which listens on TCP Port 31001 by default, by sending an
      XML request containing bogus authentication information. After sending
      this request, the server responds with the legitimate username and
      password for the service. With this information, an attacker has
      complete control over the FTP service, which includes the ability to
      add and remove FTP users, as well as add, remove, and modify
      available directories and their permissions.
auxiliary_scanner/http/titan_ftp_admin_p.name: Titan FTP Administrative Password Disclosure

auxiliary_scanner/http/xorcom_completepb.description:

          Xorcom CompletePBX <= 5.2.35. The issue occurs due to improper validation of the
          `systemDataFileName` parameter in the `diagnostics` module, allowing authenticated attackers
          to retrieve arbitrary files from the system.

          Additionally, the exploitation of this vulnerability results in the **deletion** of the
          requested file from the target system.

          The vulnerability is identified as CVE-2025-30005.

author: Valentin Lobstein
auxiliary_scanner/http/xorcom_completepb.description:

          The issue resides in the backup download function, where user input is not properly validated,
          allowing an attacker to access arbitrary files on the system as root.

          The vulnerability is triggered by setting the `backup` parameter to a Base64-encoded
          absolute file path, prefixed by a comma `,`. This results in the server exposing the
          file contents directly.

auxiliary_scanner/ike/cisco_ike_benignce.description:

          processing code in Cisco IOS, Cisco IOS XE, and Cisco IOS XR Software
          could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to retrieve memory
          contents, which could lead to the disclosure of confidential information.

          The vulnerability is due to insufficient condition checks in the part
          of the code that handles IKEv1 security negotiation requests.
          An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted IKEv1
          packet to an affected device configured to accept IKEv1 security
          negotiation requests. A successful exploit could allow the attacker
          to retrieve memory contents, which could lead to the disclosure of
          confidential information.
auxiliary_scanner/ike/cisco_ike_benignce.name: Cisco IKE Information Disclosure

auxiliary_scanner/ip/ipidseq.description:

        them using the same method Nmap uses when it's performing
        its IPID Idle Scan (-sI) and OS Detection (-O).

        Nmap's probes are SYN/ACKs while this module's are SYNs.
        While this does not change the underlying functionality,
        it does change the chance of whether or not the probe
        will be stopped by a firewall.

        Nmap's Idle Scan can use hosts whose IPID sequences are
        classified as "Incremental" or "Broken little-endian incremental".

author: Justin Cacak
auxiliary_scanner/misc/cctv_dvr_login.description:
This module tests for standalone CCTV DVR video surveillance
        deployments specifically by MicroDigital, HIVISION, CTRing, and
        numerous other rebranded devices that are utilizing default vendor
        passwords. Additionally, this module has the ability to brute
        force user accounts.

        Such CCTV DVR video surveillance deployments support remote
        viewing through Central Management Software (CMS) via the
        CMS Web Client, an IE ActiveX control hosted over HTTP, or
        through Win32 or mobile CMS client software. By default,
        remote authentication is handled over port 5920/TCP with video
        streaming over 5921/TCP.

        After successful authentication over 5920/TCP this module
        will then attempt to determine if the IE ActiveX control
        is listening on the default HTTP port (80/TCP).

This module takes advantage of a protocol design issue with the
        Ray Sharp based DVR systems. It is possible to retrieve the username and

        this platform and exposing the same issue may include Swann, Lorex,

auxiliary_scanner/misc/rosewill_rxs3211_.description:
This module takes advantage of a protocol design issue with the Rosewill admin
        executable in order to retrieve passwords, allowing remote attackers to take

        Hawking, Zonet, etc, are also believed to have the same flaw, but not fully tested.
        The protocol design issue also allows attackers to reset passwords on the device.
auxiliary_scanner/misc/rosewill_rxs3211_.name: Rosewill RXS-3211 IP Camera Password Retriever

          The vulnerability exists in the Preboot service and can be triggered by sending a specially
          crafted PROXY_CMD_FTP_FILE (opcode 0x21) packet to the 998/TCP port. This module has been

auxiliary_scanner/msmq/cve_2023_21554_qu.description:
This module checks the provided hosts for the CVE-2023-21554 vulnerability by sending
          a MSMQ message with an altered DataLength field within the SRMPEnvelopeHeader that
          overflows the given buffer. On patched systems, the error is caught and no response
          is sent back. On vulnerable systems, the integer wraps around and depending on the length
          could cause an out-of-bounds write. In the context of this module a response is sent back,
          which indicates that the system is vulnerable.
auxiliary_scanner/msmq/cve_2023_21554_qu.name: CVE-2023-21554 - QueueJumper - MSMQ RCE Check

auxiliary_scanner/mssql/mssql_hashdump.description:
This module extracts the usernames and encrypted password
        hashes from a MSSQL server and stores them for later cracking.
        This module also saves information about the server version and
        table names, which can be used to seed the wordlist.
auxiliary_scanner/mssql/mssql_hashdump.name: MSSQL Password Hashdump

auxiliary_scanner/mssql/mssql_schemadump.description:

          Instance. It will disregard builtin and example DBs such
          as master, model, msdb, and tempdb. The module will create
          a note for each DB found, and store a YAML formatted output
          as loot for easy reading.

auxiliary_scanner/mssql/mssql_version.description: Executes a TDS7 pre-login request against the MSSQL instance to query for version information.

author: theLightCosine <theLightCosine@metasploit.com>
jcran <jcran@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/mysql/mysql_authbypass.description:
This module exploits a password bypass vulnerability in MySQL in order
        to extract the usernames and encrypted password hashes from a MySQL server.
        These hashes are stored as loot for later cracking.

        Impacts MySQL versions:
        - 5.1.x before 5.1.63
        - 5.5.x before 5.5.24
        - 5.6.x before 5.6.6

        And MariaDB versions:
        - 5.1.x before 5.1.62
        - 5.2.x before 5.2.12
        - 5.3.x before 5.3.6
        - 5.5.x before 5.5.23
auxiliary_scanner/mysql/mysql_authbypass.name: MySQL Authentication Bypass Password Dump

auxiliary_scanner/nntp/nntp_login.description:
This module attempts to authenticate to NNTP services
          which support the AUTHINFO authentication extension.

          This module supports AUTHINFO USER/PASS authentication,
          but does not support AUTHINFO GENERIC or AUTHINFO SASL
          authentication methods.
auxiliary_scanner/nntp/nntp_login.name: NNTP Login Utility

author: hdm <x@hdm.io>
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_monlist.description:
This module identifies NTP servers which permit "monlist" queries and
        obtains the recent clients list. The monlist feature allows remote
        attackers to cause a denial of service (traffic amplification)
        via spoofed requests. The more clients there are in the list, the
        greater the amplification.
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_monlist.name: NTP Monitor List Scanner

author: Matthew Van Gundy of Cisco ASIG
Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_nak_to_the_fut.description:
Crypto-NAK packets can be used to cause ntpd to accept time from
          unauthenticated ephemeral symmetric peers by bypassing the
          authentication required to mobilize peer associations.  This module
          sends these Crypto-NAK packets in order to establish an association
          between the target ntpd instance and the attacking client.  The end goal
          is to cause ntpd to declare the legitimate peers "false tickers" and
          choose the attacking clients as the preferred peers, allowing
          these peers to control time.
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_nak_to_the_fut.name: NTP "NAK to the Future"

author: Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_peer_list_dos.description:
This module identifies NTP servers which permit "PEER_LIST" queries and
        return responses that are larger in size or greater in quantity than
        the request, allowing remote attackers to cause a distributed, reflected
        denial of service (aka, "DRDoS" or traffic amplification) via spoofed
        requests.
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_peer_list_dos.name: NTP Mode 7 PEER_LIST DoS Scanner

author: Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_peer_list_sum_.description:
This module identifies NTP servers which permit "PEER_LIST_SUM" queries and
        return responses that are larger in size or greater in quantity than
        the request, allowing remote attackers to cause a distributed, reflected
        denial of service (aka, "DRDoS" or traffic amplification) via spoofed
        requests.
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_peer_list_sum_.name: NTP Mode 7 PEER_LIST_SUM DoS Scanner

author: Ewerson Guimaraes(Crash) <crash@dclabs.com.br>
Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_readvar.description:
This module reads the system internal NTP variables. These variables contain
          potentially sensitive information, such as the NTP software version, operating
          system version, peers, and more.
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_readvar.name: NTP Clock Variables Disclosure

author: Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_req_nonce_dos.description:
This module identifies NTP servers which permit mode 6 REQ_NONCE requests that
        can be used to conduct DRDoS attacks. In some configurations, NTP servers will
        respond to REQ_NONCE requests with a response larger than the request,
        allowing remote attackers to cause a distributed, reflected
        denial of service (aka, "DRDoS" or traffic amplification) via spoofed
        requests.
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_req_nonce_dos.name: NTP Mode 6 REQ_NONCE DRDoS Scanner

author: Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_reslist_dos.description:
This module identifies NTP servers which permit "reslist" queries and
        obtains the list of restrictions placed on various network interfaces,
        networks or hosts. The reslist feature allows remote
        attackers to cause a distributed, reflected denial of service (aka, "DRDoS" or
        traffic amplification) via spoofed requests. The more interfaces, networks
        or hosts with specific restrictions, the greater the amplification.
        requests.
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_reslist_dos.name: NTP Mode 7 GET_RESTRICT DRDoS Scanner

author: Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_unsettrap_dos.description:
This module identifies NTP servers which permit mode 6 UNSETTRAP requests that
        can be used to conduct DRDoS attacks.  In some configurations, NTP servers will
        respond to UNSETTRAP requests with multiple packets, allowing remote attackers
        to cause a distributed, reflected denial of service (aka, "DRDoS" or traffic
        amplification) via spoofed requests.
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/ntp_unsettrap_dos.name: NTP Mode 6 UNSETTRAP DRDoS Scanner

author: Tom Tervoort
Spencer McIntyre
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/timeroast.description:
Windows authenticates NTP requests by calculating the message digest using the NT hash followed by the first
          48 bytes of the NTP message (all fields preceding the key ID). An attacker can abuse this to recover hashes
          that can be cracked offline for machine and trust accounts. The attacker must know the accounts RID, but
          because RIDs are sequential, they can easily be enumerated.
auxiliary_scanner/ntp/timeroast.name: NTP Timeroast

todb <todb@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/isqlplus_login.description:
This module attempts to authenticate against an Oracle ISQL*Plus
        administration web site using username and password combinations indicated
        by the USER_FILE, PASS_FILE, and USERPASS_FILE.

        This module does not require a valid SID, but if one is defined, it will be used.
        Works against Oracle 9.2, 10.1 & 10.2 iSQL*Plus.  This module will attempt to
        fingerprint the version and automatically select the correct POST request.
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/isqlplus_login.name: Oracle iSQL*Plus Login Utility

author: CG <cg@carnal0wnage.com>
todb <todb@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/isqlplus_sidbru.description:
This module attempts to bruteforce the SID on the Oracle application server iSQL*Plus
        login pages.  It does this by testing Oracle error responses returned in the HTTP response.
        Incorrect username/pass with a correct SID will produce an Oracle ORA-01017 error.
        Works against Oracle 9.2, 10.1 & 10.2 iSQL*Plus.  This module will attempt to
        fingerprint the version and automatically select the correct POST request.
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/isqlplus_sidbru.name: Oracle iSQLPlus SID Check

author: theLightCosine <theLightCosine@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/oracle_hashdump.description:
This module dumps the usernames and password hashes
          from Oracle given the proper Credentials and SID.
          These are then stored as creds for later cracking using auxiliary/analyze/jtr_oracle_fast.
          This module supports Oracle DB versions 8i, 9i, 10g, 11g, and 12c.
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/oracle_hashdump.name: Oracle Password Hashdump

author: Patrik Karlsson <patrik@cqure.net>
todb <todb@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/oracle_login.description:
This module attempts to authenticate against an Oracle RDBMS

author: todb <todb@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/sid_brute.description:

          instance name (also known as a SID).
          Any response other than a "reject" will be considered a success.
          If a specific SID is provided, that SID will be attempted. Otherwise,
          SIDs read from the named file will be attempted in sequence instead.

author: CG <cg@carnal0wnage.com>
MC <mc@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/sid_enum.description:

          the SID will have to be bruteforced or guessed.

author: CG <cg@carnal0wnage.com>
auxiliary_scanner/oracle/tnslsnr_version.description: This module simply queries the tnslsnr service for the Oracle build.

auxiliary_scanner/oracle/tnspoison_check.description:

          for a response indicating an error. If the registration is errored, the target is not
          vulnerable. Otherwise, the target is vulnerable to malicious registrations.

        amplification DDoS attack against a third party.

author: kris katterjohn <katterjohn@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/portscan/ack.description:
Map out firewall rulesets with a raw ACK scan.  Any
        unfiltered ports found means a stateful firewall is
        not in place for them.
auxiliary_scanner/portscan/ack.name: TCP ACK Firewall Scanner

auxiliary_scanner/portscan/ftpbounce.description:

        method.

auxiliary_scanner/portscan/syn.description: Enumerate open TCP services using a raw SYN scan.
auxiliary_scanner/portscan/syn.name: TCP SYN Port Scanner

author: hdm <x@hdm.io>
kris katterjohn <katterjohn@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/portscan/tcp.description:
Enumerate open TCP services by performing a full TCP connect on each port.
        This does not need administrative privileges on the source machine, which
        may be useful if pivoting.
auxiliary_scanner/portscan/tcp.name: TCP Port Scanner

author: kris katterjohn <katterjohn@gmail.com>
auxiliary_scanner/portscan/xmas.description:
Enumerate open|filtered TCP services using a raw
        "XMas" scan; this sends probes containing the FIN,
        PSH and URG flags.
auxiliary_scanner/portscan/xmas.name: TCP "XMas" Port Scanner

author: hdm <x@hdm.io>
auxiliary_scanner/postgres/postgres_dbna.description:
This module can identify PostgreSQL 9.0, 9.1, and 9.2 servers that are
          vulnerable to command-line flag injection through CVE-2013-1899. This
          can lead to denial of service, privilege escalation, or even arbitrary
          code execution.
auxiliary_scanner/postgres/postgres_dbna.name: PostgreSQL Database Name Command Line Flag Injection

auxiliary_scanner/postgres/postgres_hash.description:

        hashes from a Postgres server and stores them for later cracking.
auxiliary_scanner/postgres/postgres_hash.name: Postgres Password Hashdump

author: todb <todb@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/postgres/postgres_logi.description:
This module attempts to authenticate against a PostgreSQL
          instance using username and password combinations indicated
          by the USER_FILE, PASS_FILE, and USERPASS_FILE options. Note that
          passwords may be either plaintext or MD5 formatted hashes.
auxiliary_scanner/postgres/postgres_logi.name: PostgreSQL Login Utility

auxiliary_scanner/postgres/postgres_sche.description:

auxiliary_scanner/postgres/postgres_vers.description: Enumerates the version of PostgreSQL servers.

author: National Cyber Security Centre
JaGoTu
zerosum0x0
Tom Sellers
auxiliary_scanner/rdp/cve_2019_0708_blue.description:
This module checks a range of hosts for the CVE-2019-0708 vulnerability
          by binding the MS_T120 channel outside of its normal slot and sending
          non-DoS packets which respond differently on patched and vulnerable hosts.
          It can optionally trigger the DoS vulnerability.
auxiliary_scanner/rdp/cve_2019_0708_blue.name: CVE-2019-0708 BlueKeep Microsoft Remote Desktop RCE Check

Brandon McCann "zeknox" <bmccann@accuvant.com>

This module checks a range of hosts for the MS12-020 vulnerability.
          This does not cause a DoS on the target.
auxiliary_scanner/rdp/ms12_020_check.name: MS12-020 Microsoft Remote Desktop Checker

author: Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/rdp/rdp_scanner.description:
This module attempts to connect to the specified Remote Desktop Protocol port
          and determines if it speaks RDP.

          When available, the Credential Security Support Provider (CredSSP) protocol will be used to identify the
          version of Windows on which the server is running. Enabling the DETECT_NLA option will cause a second
          connection to be made to the server to identify if Network Level Authentication (NLA) is required.
auxiliary_scanner/rdp/rdp_scanner.name: Identify endpoints speaking the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP)

author: Nixawk
Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
auxiliary_scanner/redis/file_upload.description:
This module can be used to leverage functionality exposed by Redis to
          achieve somewhat arbitrary file upload to a file and directory to
          which the user account running the redis instance has access.  It is
          not totally arbitrary because the exact contents of the file cannot
          be completely controlled given the nature of how Redis stores its
          database on disk.
auxiliary_scanner/redis/file_upload.name: Redis File Upload

author: Nixawk
auxiliary_scanner/redis/redis_login.description: This module attempts to authenticate to an Redis service.
auxiliary_scanner/redis/redis_login.name: Redis Login Utility

Nixawk
auxiliary_scanner/redis/redis_server.description:
This module locates Redis endpoints by attempting to run a specified
          Redis command.
auxiliary_scanner/redis/redis_server.name: Redis Command Execute Scanner

author: hdm <x@hdm.io>
auxiliary_scanner/rogue/rogue_recv.description:
This module listens for replies to the requests sent by
      the rogue_send module. The RPORT, CPORT, and ECHOID values
      must match the rogue_send parameters used exactly.
auxiliary_scanner/rogue/rogue_recv.name: Rogue Gateway Detection: Receiver

author: hdm <x@hdm.io>
auxiliary_scanner/rogue/rogue_send.description:
This module send a series of TCP SYN and ICMP ECHO requests
      to each internal target host, spoofing the source address of an external
      system running the rogue_recv module. This allows the system running
      the rogue_recv module to determine what external IP a given internal
      system is using as its default route.
auxiliary_scanner/rogue/rogue_send.name: Rogue Gateway Detection: Sender

author: jduck <jduck@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/rservices/rexec_login.description:
This module will test an rexec service on a range of machines and
        report successful logins.

        NOTE: This module requires access to bind to privileged ports (below 1024).
auxiliary_scanner/rservices/rexec_login.name: rexec Authentication Scanner

author: jduck <jduck@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/rservices/rlogin_login.description:
This module will test an rlogin service on a range of machines and
        report successful logins.

        NOTE: This module requires access to bind to privileged ports (below 1024).
auxiliary_scanner/rservices/rlogin_login.name: rlogin Authentication Scanner

author: jduck <jduck@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/rservices/rsh_login.description:

        report successful logins.

        NOTE: This module requires access to bind to privileged ports (below 1024).
auxiliary_scanner/rservices/rsh_login.name: rsh Authentication Scanner

author: ikkini
Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
Nixawk
auxiliary_scanner/rsync/modules_list.description:
An rsync module is essentially a directory share.  These modules can
        optionally be protected by a password.  This module connects to and
        negotiates with an rsync server, lists the available modules and,
        optionally, determines if the module requires a password to access.
auxiliary_scanner/rsync/modules_list.name: List Rsync Modules

author: Jonathan Peterson <deadjakk@shell.rip>
auxiliary_scanner/sage/x3_adxsrv_login.description:
This module allows an attacker to perform a password guessing attack against
        the Sage X3 AdxAdmin service, which in turn can be used to authenticate to
        a local Windows account.

        This module implements the X3Crypt function to 'encrypt' any passwords to
        be used during the authentication process, given a plaintext password.
auxiliary_scanner/sage/x3_adxsrv_login.name: Sage X3 AdxAdmin Login Scanner

author: Alexandr Polyakov
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_ctc_verb_tampe.description:
This module exploits an authentication bypass vulnerability in SAP NetWeaver
        CTC service. The service is vulnerable to verb tampering allowing for unauthorised
        OS user management. Information about resolution should be available at SAP notes
        1589525 and 1624450 (authentication required).
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_ctc_verb_tampe.name: SAP CTC Service Verb Tampering User Management

author: Bruno Morisson <bm@integrity.pt>
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_hostctrl_getco.description:

        information from Host Agent through the SAP HostControl service.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_hostctrl_getco.name: SAP Host Agent Information Disclosure

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
ChrisJohnRiley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_icf_public_inf.description:
This module uses the /sap/public/info service within SAP Internet Communication
        Framework (ICF) to obtain the operating system version, SAP version, IP address
        and other information.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_icf_public_inf.name: SAP ICF /sap/public/info Service Sensitive Information Gathering

author: Chris John Riley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_icm_urlscan.description:
This module scans for commonly found SAP Internet Communication Manager URLs
          and outputs return codes for the user.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_icm_urlscan.name: SAP URL Scanner

author: Chris John Riley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_abapl.description: This module simply attempts to extract the ABAP syslog through the SAP Management Console SOAP Interface.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_abapl.name: SAP Management Console ABAP Syslog Disclosure

author: Chris John Riley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_brute.description:
This module simply attempts to brute force the username and
        password for the SAP Management Console SOAP Interface. If
        the SAP_SID value is set it will replace instances of <SAPSID>
        in any user/pass from any wordlist.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_brute.name: SAP Management Console Brute Force

author: Chris John Riley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_extra.description:
This module simply attempts to extract SAP users from the ABAP
        Syslog through the SAP Management Console SOAP Interface.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_extra.name: SAP Management Console Extract Users

author: Chris John Riley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_getac.description:
This module simply attempts to output a list of SAP access points through the
        SAP Management Console SOAP Interface.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_getac.name: SAP Management Console Get Access Points

author: Chris John Riley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_geten.description:
This module simply attempts to identify SAP Environment
        settings through the SAP Management Console SOAP Interface.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_geten.name: SAP Management Console getEnvironment

author: Chris John Riley
Bruno Morisson <bm@integrity.pt>
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_getlo.description:
This module simply attempts to download available logfiles and
        developer tracefiles through the SAP Management Console SOAP
        Interface. Please use the sap_mgmt_con_listlogfiles
        extension to view a list of available files.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_getlo.name: SAP Management Console Get Logfile

author: Chris John Riley
Bruno Morisson <bm@integrity.pt>
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_getpr.description: This module attempts to list SAP processes through the SAP Management Console SOAP Interface
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_getpr.name: SAP Management Console GetProcessList

author: Chris John Riley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_getpr.description:
This module simply attempts to output a SAP process parameters and
        configuration settings through the SAP Management Console SOAP Interface.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_getpr.name: SAP Management Console Get Process Parameters

author: Chris John Riley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_insta.description:
This module simply attempts to identify the instance properties
        through the SAP Management Console SOAP Interface.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_insta.name: SAP Management Console Instance Properties

author: Chris John Riley
Jacobo Avariento Gimeno
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_listc.description:
This module attempts to list the config files
          through the SAP Management Console SOAP Interface.
          Returns a list of config files found in the SAP configuration with its
          absolute paths inside the server filesystem.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_listc.name: SAP Management Console List Config Files

author: Chris John Riley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_listl.description:
This module simply attempts to output a list of available

        Console SOAP Interface.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_listl.name: SAP Management Console List Logfiles

auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_start.description:

auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_mgmt_con_versi.description:

author: Mariano Nunez
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_router_info_re.description: Display the remote connection table from a SAPRouter.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_router_info_re.name: SAPRouter Admin Request

author: Bruno Morisson <bm@integrity.pt>
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_router_portsca.description:
This module maps ACLs and identifies open/closed ports accessible
        on hosts through a saprouter.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_router_portsca.name: SAPRouter Port Scanner

author: Alexey Tyurin
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_smb_relay.description:
This module exploits provides several SMB Relay abuse through different SAP
        services and functions. The attack is done through specially crafted requests
        including a UNC path which will be accessing by the SAP system while trying to
        process the request.  In order to get the hashes the auxiliary/server/capture/smb
        module can be used.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_smb_relay.name: SAP SMB Relay Abuse

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_bapi_user.description:
This module makes use of the BAPI_USER_CREATE1 function, through the SOAP
        /sap/bc/soap/rfc service, for creating/modifying users on a SAP.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_bapi_user.name: SAP /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP Service BAPI_USER_CREATE1 Function User Creation

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_brute.description:
This module attempts to brute force SAP username and passwords through the
        /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP service, using RFC_PING function.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_brute.name: SAP SOAP Service RFC_PING Login Brute Forcer

author: nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_dbmcl.description:
This module makes use of the SXPG_CALL_SYSTEM Remote Function Call, through the
        use of the /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP service, to inject and execute OS commands.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_dbmcl.name: SAP /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP Service SXPG_CALL_SYSTEM Function Command Injection

author: nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_dbmcl.description:
This module makes use of the SXPG_COMMAND_EXEC Remote Function Call, through the
        use of the /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP service, to inject and execute OS commands.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_dbmcl.name: SAP /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP Service SXPG_COMMAND_EXEC Function Command Injection

author: nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_eps_g.description:
This module abuses the SAP NetWeaver EPS_GET_DIRECTORY_LISTING function, on the
        SAP SOAP RFC Service, to check for remote directory existence and get the number
        of entries on it. The module can also be used to capture SMB hashes by using a fake
        SMB share as DIR.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_eps_g.name: SAP SOAP RFC EPS_GET_DIRECTORY_LISTING Directories Information Disclosure

author: lexey Tyurin
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_pfl_c.description:
This module abuses the SAP NetWeaver PFL_CHECK_OS_FILE_EXISTENCE function, on
        the SAP SOAP RFC Service, to check for files existence on the remote file system.
        The module can also be used to capture SMB hashes by using a fake SMB share as
        FILEPATH.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_pfl_c.name: SAP SOAP RFC PFL_CHECK_OS_FILE_EXISTENCE File Existence Check

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_ping.description:
This module makes use of the RFC_PING function, through the	/sap/bc/soap/rfc
        SOAP service, to test connectivity to remote RFC destinations.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_ping.name: SAP /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP Service RFC_PING Function Service Discovery

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_read_.description:
This module uses the RFC_READ_TABLE function to read data from tables using
        the /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP service.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_read_.name: SAP /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP Service RFC_READ_TABLE Function Dump Data

author: Alexey Tyurin
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_rzl_r.description:
This module exploits the SAP NetWeaver RZL_READ_DIR_LOCAL function, on the SAP
        SOAP RFC Service, to enumerate directory contents. It returns only the first 32
        characters of the filename since they are truncated. The module can also be used to
        capture SMB hashes by using a fake SMB share as DIR.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_rzl_r.name: SAP SOAP RFC RZL_READ_DIR_LOCAL Directory Contents Listing

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_susr_.description:
This module makes use of the SUSR_RFC_USER_INTERFACE function, through the SOAP
        /sap/bc/soap/rfc service, for creating/modifying users on a SAP.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_susr_.name: SAP /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP Service SUSR_RFC_USER_INTERFACE Function User Creation

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_sxpg_.description:
This module makes use of the SXPG_CALL_SYSTEM Remote Function Call, through the
        use of the /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP service to execute OS commands as configured in
        the SM69 transaction.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_sxpg_.name: SAP /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP Service SXPG_CALL_SYSTEM Function Command Execution

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_sxpg_.description:
This module makes use of the SXPG_COMMAND_EXECUTE Remote Function Call, through
        the use of the /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP service to execute OS commands as configured
        in the SM69 transaction.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_sxpg_.name: SAP SOAP RFC SXPG_COMMAND_EXECUTE

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
ChrisJohnRiley
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_syste.description:
This module makes use of the RFC_SYSTEM_INFO Function to obtain the operating
        system version, SAP version, IP address and other information through the use of
        the /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP service.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_rfc_syste.name: SAP /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP Service RFC_SYSTEM_INFO Function Sensitive Information Gathering

author: Agnivesh Sathasivam
nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_th_saprel.description:
This module attempts to identify software, OS and DB versions through the SAP
        function TH_SAPREL using the /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP service.
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_soap_th_saprel.name: SAP /sap/bc/soap/rfc SOAP Service TH_SAPREL Function Information Disclosure

author: nmonkee
auxiliary_scanner/sap/sap_web_gui_brute_.description:
This module attempts to brute force SAP username and passwords through the SAP Web
        GUI service. Default clients can be	tested without needing to set a CLIENT. Common
        and default user/password combinations can be tested just setting the DEFAULT_CRED
        variable to true. The MSF_DATA_DIRECTORY/wordlists/sap_default.txt path store
        stores these default combinations.

juan vazquez <juan.vazquez@metasploit.com>
auxiliary_scanner/scada/indusoft_ntwebse.description:
This module exploits a directory traversal vulnerability in Indusoft WebStudio.
        The vulnerability exists in the NTWebServer component and allows to read arbitrary
        remote files with the privileges of the NTWebServer process. The module has been
        tested successfully on Indusoft WebStudio 6.1 SP6.

author: K. Reid Wightman <wightman@digitalbond.com>

auxiliary_scanner/scada/koyo_login.description:
This module attempts to authenticate to a locked Koyo DirectLogic PLC.
        The PLC uses a restrictive passcode, which can be A0000000 through A9999999.
        The "A" prefix can also be changed by the administrator to any other character,
        which can be set through the PREFIX option of this module.

        This module is based on the original 'koyobrute.rb' Basecamp module from

author: Juan Escobar <juan@null-life.com>
Ezequiel Fernandez
auxiliary_scanner/scada/modbus_banner_gr.description:
This module grabs the banner of any device running the Modbus protocol
          by sending a request with Modbus Function Code 43 (Read Device
          Identification). Modbus is a data communications protocol originally
          published by Modicon (now Schneider Electric) in 1979 for use with its
          programmable logic controllers (PLCs).
auxiliary_scanner/scada/modbus_banner_gr.name: Modbus Banner Grabbing

author: EsMnemon <esm@mnemonic.no>
auxiliary_scanner/scada/modbus_finduniti.description:
Modbus is a cleartext protocol used in common SCADA systems, developed
          originally as a serial-line (RS232) async protocol, and later transformed
          to IP, which is called ModbusTCP. default tcp port is 502.

          This module sends a command (0x04, read input register) to the modbus endpoint.
          If this command is sent to the correct unit-id, it returns with the same function-id.
          if not, it should be added 0x80, so that it sys 0x84, and an exception-code follows
          which do not interest us. This does not always happen, but at least the first 4
          bytes in the return-packet should be exact the same as what was sent.

          You can change port, ip and the scan-range for unit-id. There is also added a
          value - BENICE - to make the scanner sleep a second or more between probes. We
          have seen installations where scanning too many too fast works like a DoS.
auxiliary_scanner/scada/modbus_finduniti.name: Modbus Unit ID and Station ID Enumerator

author: Patrick DeSantis <p@t-r10t.com>
auxiliary_scanner/scada/moxa_discover.description:
The Moxa protocol listens on 4800/UDP and will respond to broadcast
          or direct traffic.  The service is known to be used on Moxa devices
          in the NPort, OnCell, and MGate product lines.

          A discovery packet compels a Moxa device to respond to the sender
          with some basic device information that is needed for more advanced
          functions.  The discovery data is 8 bytes in length and is the most
          basic example of the Moxa protocol.  It may be sent out as a
          broadcast (destination 255.255.255.255) or to an individual device.

          Devices that respond to this query may be vulnerable to serious
          information disclosure vulnerabilities, such as CVE-2016-9361.

          The module is the work of Patrick DeSantis of Cisco Talos and is
          derived from original work by K. Reid Wightman. Tested and validated
          on a Moxa NPort 6250 with firmware versions 1.13 and 1.15.
auxiliary_scanner/scada/moxa_discover.name: Moxa UDP Device Discovery

author: Luis Rosa <lmrosa@dei.uc.pt>
auxiliary_scanner/scada/pcomclient.description:
Unitronics Vision PLCs allow unauthenticated PCOM commands
          to query PLC registers.
auxiliary_scanner/scada/pcomclient.name: Unitronics PCOM Client

author: Tijl Deneut <tijl.deneut@howest.be>
auxiliary_scanner/scada/profinet_siemens.description:
This module will use Layer2 packets, known as Profinet Discovery packets,
        to detect all Siemens (and sometimes other) devices on a network.
        It is perfectly SCADA-safe, as there will only be ONE single packet sent out.
        Devices will respond with their IP configuration and hostnames.
        Created by XiaK Industrial Security Research Center (www[dot]xiak[dot]be))

auxiliary_scanner/smb/psexec_loggedin_us.description:
This module uses a valid administrator username and password to enumerate users

author: Joshua D. Abraham <jabra@praetorian.com>
auxiliary_scanner/smb/smb_enum_gpp.description:
This module enumerates files from target domain controllers and connects to them via SMB.
        It then looks for Group Policy Preference XML files containing local/domain user accounts
        and passwords and decrypts them using Microsoft's public AES key. This module has been
        tested successfully on a Win2k8 R2 Domain Controller.

nebulus
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
r3dy
altonjx
sjanusz-r7
auxiliary_scanner/smb/smb_enumshares.description:
This module determines what shares are provided by the SMB service and which ones
          are readable/writable. It also collects additional information such as share types,

          By default, a RubySMB net_share_enum_all request is done in order to retrieve share information,

auxiliary_scanner/smb/smb_lookupsid.description:

        ACTION to either LOCAL or DOMAIN
auxiliary_scanner/smb/smb_lookupsid.name: SMB SID User Enumeration (LookupSid)

author: Sean Dillon <sean.dillon@risksense.com>
Luke Jennings
auxiliary_scanner/smb/smb_ms17_010.description:
Uses information disclosure to determine if MS17-010 has been patched or not.
          Specifically, it connects to the IPC$ tree and attempts a transaction on FID 0.
          If the status returned is "STATUS_INSUFF_SERVER_RESOURCES", the machine does
          not have the MS17-010 patch.

          If the machine is missing the MS17-010 patch, the module will check for an
          existing DoublePulsar (ring 0 shellcode/malware) infection.

          This module does not require valid SMB credentials in default server
          configurations. It can log on as the user "\" and connect to IPC$.
auxiliary_scanner/smb/smb_ms17_010.name: MS17-010 SMB RCE Detection

auxiliary_scanner/smb/smb_uninit_cred.description: This module checks if a Samba target is vulnerable to an uninitialized variable creds vulnerability.

auxiliary_scanner/smb/smb_version.description:
Fingerprint and display version information about SMB servers. Protocol
        information and host operating system (if available) will be reported.

        version 1 of the SMB protocol. Compression and encryption capability
        negotiation is only present in version 3.1.1.
auxiliary_scanner/smb/smb_version.name: SMB Version Detection

author: Heyder Andrade <heyder@alligatorteam.org>
nebulus
auxiliary_scanner/smtp/smtp_enum.description:
The SMTP service has two internal commands that allow the enumeration
        of users: VRFY (confirming the names of valid users) and EXPN (which
        reveals the actual address of users aliases and lists of e-mail
        (mailing lists)). Through the implementation of these SMTP commands can
        reveal a list of valid users.

auxiliary_scanner/smtp/smtp_ntlm_domain.description: Extract the Windows domain name from an SMTP NTLM challenge.

author: Campbell Murray

auxiliary_scanner/smtp/smtp_relay.description:

        Some of the extended methods will try to abuse configuration or mailserver flaws.
auxiliary_scanner/smtp/smtp_relay.name: SMTP Open Relay Detection

auxiliary_scanner/snmp/arris_dg950.description:

auxiliary_scanner/snmp/brocade_enumhash.description:

author: pello <fropert@packetfault.org>
hdm <x@hdm.io>
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/cisco_config_tftp.description:
This module will download the startup or running configuration
        from a Cisco IOS device using SNMP and TFTP. A read-write SNMP
        community is required. The SNMP community scanner module can
        assist in identifying a read-write community. The target must
        be able to connect back to the Metasploit system and the use of
        NAT will cause the TFTP transfer to fail.
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/cisco_config_tftp.name: Cisco IOS SNMP Configuration Grabber (TFTP)

author: pello <fropert@packetfault.org>
ct5595
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/cisco_upload_file.description:
This module will copy file to a Cisco IOS device using SNMP and TFTP.
        The action Override_Config will override the running config of the Cisco device.
        A read-write SNMP community is required. The SNMP community scanner module can
        assist in identifying a read-write community. The target must
        be able to connect back to the Metasploit system and the use of
        NAT will cause the TFTP transfer to fail.
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/cisco_upload_file.name: Cisco IOS SNMP File Upload (TFTP)

author: Karn Ganeshen
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/cnpilot_r_snmp_lo.description:
Cambium cnPilot r200/r201 devices can be administered using SNMP. The
        device configuration contains IP addresses, keys, passwords, & lots of juicy
        information. This module exploits an access control flaw, which allows remotely
        extracting sensitive information such as account passwords, WiFI PSK, & SIP
        credentials via SNMP Read-Only (RO) community string.
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/cnpilot_r_snmp_lo.name: Cambium cnPilot r200/r201 SNMP Enumeration

author: Karn Ganeshen
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/epmp1000_snmp_loo.description:
Cambium devices (ePMP, PMP, Force, & others) can be administered using
        SNMP. The device configuration contains IP addresses, keys, and passwords,
        amongst other information. This module uses SNMP to extract Cambium ePMP device
        configuration. On certain software versions, specific device configuration
        values can be accessed using SNMP RO string, even though only SNMP RW string
        should be able to access them, according to MIB documentation. The module also
        triggers full configuration backup, and retrieves the backup url. The
        configuration file can then be downloaded without authentication. The module
        has been tested on Cambium ePMP versions 3.5 & prior.
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/epmp1000_snmp_loo.name: Cambium ePMP 1000 SNMP Enumeration

author: Deral "PercentX" Heiland
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/netopia_enum.description:
This module extracts WEP keys and WPA preshared keys from
        certain Netopia cable modems.
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/netopia_enum.name: Netopia 3347 Cable Modem Wifi Enumeration

author: Matthew Kienow <mkienow@inokii.com>
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/sbg6580_enum.description:
This module allows SNMP enumeration of the ARRIS / Motorola
          SURFboard SBG6580 Series Wi-Fi Cable Modem Gateway. It supports the username
          and password for the device user interface as well as wireless network keys
          and information.
          The default community used is "public".
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/sbg6580_enum.name: ARRIS / Motorola SBG6580 Cable Modem SNMP Enumeration Module

author: Matteo Cantoni <goony@nothink.org>
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/snmp_enum.description:
This module allows enumeration of any devices with SNMP
          protocol support. It supports hardware, software, and network information.
          The default community used is "public".
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/snmp_enum.name: SNMP Enumeration Module

author: Matteo Cantoni <goony@nothink.org>
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/snmp_enum_hp_lase.description:

          The default community used is "public".

auxiliary_scanner/snmp/snmp_enumshares.description: This module will use LanManager OID values to enumerate SMB shares on a Windows system via SNMP
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/snmp_enumshares.name: SNMP Windows SMB Share Enumeration

author: tebo <tebo@attackresearch.com>
auxiliary_scanner/snmp/snmp_enumusers.description:
This module will use LanManager/psProcessUsername OID values to
